claims.text: At stage-3 DonHang.Payments is the only service that calls the payment gateway.
A quality attribute scenario states one quality requirement as a checkable situation: trigger, conditions, required response, and how the response is measured.
YC-7 (refund-requirements.md @ stage-3 lines 43-44): a customer's refund request is received and answered within 2 seconds, even when the payment gateway does not answer or reports an error.
A requirement missing its trigger, conditions or measure cannot settle whether a design meets it; real requirements rarely label the four parts, and parts may share one phrase.

YC-10 (lines 49-50): when the gateway fails, the request is sent again automatically for at least 24 hours before it is handed to staff. YC-8 (45-46): who asked and when are never changed or deleted. YC-9 (47-48): an order is never refunded twice, even when sending to the gateway is retried.

ADR 0003's context (lines 13-15) restates YC-7, YC-9 and YC-10 before the options; lines 15-17 say the gateway key and money records are the most sensitive part and, in design version 1, every copy of DonHang.Api held the key and could read/write payments.

One scenario serves comparing designs, writing a fitness function and reviewing an architecture, because each needs to know exactly what must hold; an architecture review later in this module walks through scenarios.

Trade-offs: a wish is cheap but cannot compare designs or yield a check; a scenario costs agreement on case and number with the need's owner; scenarios for every imaginable case drown those that matter. Write the scenario when a design choice depends on it.

If a stakeholder asks for 'highly available', ask which request, under which failure, measured how; if no number exists yet, record the measure as an open question with its owner; if two scenarios conflict, keep both and name the conflict.
refund-requirements.md @ stage-3 has an open-questions table (with who answers) after YC-10, at lines 52-59.

A user story states what a user wants and why (a feature); a scenario states how well the system responds in a stated case, with a measure. YC-8 keeps records intact for accounting (yes/no measure); ease of change can get a measure, e.g. services one change touches.

claims.text: Placing an order (POST /api/v1/orders) by a signed-in customer is answered with 201 (created) at stage-3; DonHang.Notifications is the service that sends order emails.
While the refund saga runs, the order holds the status `refunding`.
